claims.claim: **HAE angioedema is non-pitting swelling without urticaria, itching or redness.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **At any age, laryngeal oedema may threaten life.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Each child with an HAE diagnosis needs their own ASCIA HAE management plan**, setting out when and how attacks are treated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Adrenaline, corticosteroids and antihistamines play no part in treating HAE angioedema.** Early specific treatment improves outcomes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: HAE is autosomal dominant: **Type 1** is an absolute C1-INH deficiency (85% of cases), **Type 2** a functional one.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Presentations:** cutaneous swelling in over 90% — face, genitals and limbs (hands and feet above all) · upper airway swelling (tongue, soft palate, larynx), which can be life-threatening · abdominal pain with nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea, which can cause dehydration and collapse · a non-pruritic erythema marginatum rash in about one third.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **An attack usually peaks by 24 hours and settles over 48–72 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Triggers:** injury (dental or other surgery included), psychological stress, infection, medications (ACE inhibitors and oestrogen-containing ones especially), menstruation, vigorous exercise, certain foods — or none.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Symptoms typically start between 5 and 11 years (40% by age 5) and may worsen in adolescence. **A family history is present in 75%.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Examine the airway:** tongue, soft palate, uvula; laryngeal oedema signs — stridor, hoarseness, drooling, altered voice. **Swelling behind the teeth progresses to airway obstruction more readily than swelling in front of them.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Redness or itching suggests a diagnosis other than HAE.** Differentials: allergic reactions and anaphylaxis, idiopathic, drug-induced and (exceedingly rare in childhood) acquired angioedema.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected acute attack with no prior HAE diagnosis: check C4.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Whether to treat an attack that does not threaten life is for the child and parent to decide. **Options: subcutaneous icatibant, or intravenous C1 esterase inhibitor concentrate.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First line — C1-INH concentrate (Berinert®), any age: 20 international units/kg (round to the nearest 500 units), given as a slow IV injection at 4 mL/min.** Symptoms usually stabilise in 30 minutes; a second dose is seldom required but can follow 30 min to 2 hours after the first (<1% relapse). Do not shake the solution.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Icatibant, slow SC injection:** under 12 kg or under 2 years — seek Immunology advice; **10 mg (1 mL) for 12–25 kg · 15 mg (1.5 mL) for 26–40 kg · 20 mg (2 mL) for 41–50 kg · 30 mg (3 mL) over 50 kg**. A repeat dose is possible 6 hours after the first (<10% relapse); **max 3 doses/24 hours**. Injection-site reactions are usually mild.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Airway attack unresponsive to icatibant: give C1-INH concentrate as rescue.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No response after 2 hours: reconsider the diagnosis** and look for other causes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second line, used only when neither of the above is available: FFP treated with solvent/detergent**, for severe abdominal and/or laryngeal attacks — it may paradoxically worsen angioedema. Consult immunology/haematology, but don't delay in an emergency with no alternative. Adverse effects: commonly nausea, pruritus, rash; rarely allergic reactions, bronchospasm, cardiorespiratory collapse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **An airway/laryngeal attack is a medical emergency: give icatibant or C1-INH concentrate at once.** If obstruction appears imminent → senior, ICU and anaesthetic involvement, ideally including people skilled in surgical airway and fibre-optic-guided intubation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Peripheral swelling:** treat significant pain or disability, or angioedema of the face or genitals; mild swelling that doesn't affect function may not need treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Abdominal attack with moderate–severe pain, vomiting and/or distension: give C1-INH concentrate**; consider fluid resuscitation if severe. Mild pain: simple analgesia including NSAIDs.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team:** a first swelling episode or no prior diagnosis · airway/laryngeal attack · medication not working within 2 hours · relapse after first-line treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transfer:** airway/laryngeal attack (usually needs PICU/HDU observation) · immediately life-threatening situation · care beyond the hospital's comfort level · inadequate response to acute treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge:** after successful emergency treatment, children improving from peripheral or abdominal attacks may go home even if peripheral swelling has not fully resolved. **Every child diagnosed with HAE needs an allergy/immunology consultation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Short-term prophylaxis — first line, at any age: C1-INH concentrate (Berinert® IV) 20 units/kg rounded to the nearest 500 units, 1–6 hours before any medical, surgical or dental procedure.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second line, used only when first-line prophylaxis cannot be obtained: icatibant slow SC**, 2 years and over (under 2: seek Immunology advice), under 30 minutes before the procedure; keep an additional dose for emergency and **observe for over 12 hours** afterwards. Doses: seek Immunology advice under 12 kg; 10 mg (1 mL) for 12–25 kg; 15 mg (1.5 mL) for 26–40 kg; 20 mg (2 mL) for 41–50 kg; 30 mg (3 mL) over 50 kg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Long-term prophylaxis** is prescribed by the child's immunologist: lanadelumab, garadacimab, oral tranexamic acid, or C1-INH concentrate given subcutaneously (Berinert® SC).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-acute screening, with an immunologist:** serum C4, C1-INH level and C1 functional assay; **two sets at least 3 months apart**, with at least 1 set after the age of 1 (results are hard to interpret under 1 year). Genetic testing is not usually needed. **Screen the family if confirmed.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Type 1:** C1-INH function, C1-INH protein and C4 all low. **Type 2:** C1-INH function low, C1-INH protein normal or raised, C4 low.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency)' (Last updated May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hereditary_angioedema_(C1-esterase_inhibitor_deficiency)/, retrieved 2026-09-23
